messages:
Maya: quick question — saw a brief stale-read window during a prefix demote + compaction run on staging. small repro: hot prefix gets demoted, compaction launches, a few reads returned older values for ~100ms before epoch advanced. logs attached inline:

Maya: ```
[compactor] demote start prefix=tenant42:hot epoch=100 -> target=demote-slab
[read] t=1712349991.150 prefix=tenant42:hot epoch=100 -> cache miss -> tombstone fallback read ok
[read] t=1712349991.180 prefix=tenant42:hot epoch=99 -> served stale value (old kv)
[compactor] demote finish prefix=tenant42:hot epoch=100 -> tombstone=marker-1712349991
```

Maya: is this expected because reads racing a demote+compact can see pre-demote view, or is our demote ordering failing to publish a fence?

Jared: pinged. my hunch: compaction is doing two steps (copy out, then swap pointer) and reads can race the swap if they read a lower epoch key reference. we currently rely on epoch bump to reconcile but there's a tiny window.

Priya: agree with Jared. we discussed previously adding an atomic pointer swap or publishing a demote-intent marker before compaction so readers can check and wait. but that adds latency for reads that race.

Theo: could we instead make readers check generation tags on the prefix and, if mismatch, consult the compaction index (fast path) then retry? cheaper than a global quiesce.

Maya: interesting. generation tag check would be a single CAS-like read of metadata before serving from cache. if mismatch -> sync to compactor log and retry. how expensive is that in p99?

Jared: local read of prefix-metadata is O(1) in memcache, <1ms usually. retry path hits a read-through which is the common expensive case anyway. cost looks acceptable for rare races.

Priya: downside: adds complexity and more codepaths. also need to ensure metadata updates are linearizable with demote completion. currently demote finish sets tombstone marker, but pointer swap happens slightly later. reorder might be needed.

Maya: sketching invariants: 1) readers must never serve data older than last published demote epoch for that prefix. 2) demote must publish a visibility epoch before any pointer update that would remove the old copy.

Theo: if we make demote publish visibility epoch first and then perform pointer swap, readers can see the epoch and either wait or trigger a quick refresh. avoids tombstone races.

Jared: small implementation plan: (a) introduce prefix-metadata.generation (int) bumped by demote start, (b) demote writes generation->pending state, (c) compactor completes swap and writes generation->committed. readers that see pending can either wait short spin or perform synchronous fetch.

Priya: for durability and cross-node, generation changes must be written to the same consensus log as leases or we get split-brain. think we need to piggyback on lease epoch increments or use a tiny consensus write.

Maya: ok. TL;DR proposal: add prefix generation marker + small commit protocol so demote visibility is published before removal. add a targeted smoke test that injects read-after-demote races.

deploy-bot: smoke test run: demote-race-smoke v1 -> failing 2/50 (stale served). attached stack traces.

Maya: thanks bot. I'll add a follow-up RFC with sketches and perf numbers. assigning to Jared/ Priya for implementation spike.

Jared: I'll spike this week, measure extra per-read cost and retry tail.

Priya: I'll prototype consensus write for generation updates and a canary for multi-node correctness.

Theo: I'll add a targeted chaos test to simulate compaction timing on CI.

Maya: awesome. leaving TODO: spike -> perf numbers -> RFC -> smoke tests. :+1:
